adjudication_records.issue_text: In `group_member.hbs`, the `member` loop variable is not in scope inside the `itemView` template, causing `undefined` references and breaking avatar rendering, username display, and the remove action.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/templates/group.hbs` the list is rendered with `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, but the separate `group_member.hbs` itemView template references `member` (`{{avatar member}}`, `{{member.username}}`, `{{action "removeMember" member}}`). The itemView (`admin/views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define a `member` property, and Ember’s collection/itemView context is typically the item itself (accessible as `this`/direct properties or `view.content`), not a `member` variable from the outer `each` block. As written, `member` will be undefined in the itemView template, breaking avatar/username rendering and passing `undefined` to the remove action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route parameter mismatch in add_members and remove_member actions using params.require(:group_id) instead of params[:id]
findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when group name is empty
totalPages pagination off-by-one error using Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). This overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50 => floor(2)+1 = 3 pages, but only 2 pages exist). The related `next` action can set `offset` to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` then queries with `offset = user_count`, which will return an empty member list—consistent with the off-by-one page count. Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and also preventing `offset == user_count`) would avoid the extra empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Usernames input not cleared after adding members in the addMembers action

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and then only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `this.usernames` (e.g., to `null`/`""`). Since the `user-selector` component in `group.hbs` is bound to `usernames=usernames`, the input value will remain after adding members unless the component clears it internally (not shown in this diff). The diff itself provides no clearing behavior, so the finding is verifiable from the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No error handling on addMembers and removeMember model methods AJAX calls

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addMembers` and `removeMember` in `discourse/models/group.js` returning `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without a `.catch`/rejection handler, and the controller actions call them without handling failures. However, this is not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the methods return the promise so callers/framework-level AJAX error handling can deal with failures (common in Discourse/Ember apps), and the absence of local error handling is an improvement suggestion rather than a demonstrable bug/security/correctness issue from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Invalid usernames silently ignored in add_members controller action with no feedback to the client

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. When the username is invalid/nonexistent, it is simply skipped with no error collection or response indicating partial failure; the action still returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. This means invalid usernames are silently ignored with no feedback to the client, as described.

In the provided spec changes, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified/added-to; there are no corresponding tests added for the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to validate pagination behavior or the new response format. This is a concrete, verifiable test coverage gap introduced by the change.

However, the absence of a loading indicator is a UX enhancement request, not a clear correctness/bug/security defect introduced by the diff (Ember will simply render nothing until `members` is populated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent membership mutation between `add_members` (using `group.add(user)`) and `remove_member` (using `group.users.delete(user_id)`), which could lead to divergent behavior.
N+1 query pattern in add_members runs one query per username inside a loop; should batch the query

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop calls `User.find_by_username(username)`, which issues a separate DB query per username. That is a verifiable per-item query pattern introduced/retained by this diff and could be batched with a single `where(username: ...)` lookup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Extra group.save in remove_member after collection.delete re-runs group-level validations and can cause unrelated 422 errors

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which immediately removes the join record in Rails) and then conditionally renders success only if `group.save` succeeds. That `save` is not required for the membership removal and can introduce an unrelated failure mode: if the Group record fails validations/callbacks for any reason, the action will return `render_json_error(group)` (422-style error payload) even though the member was already removed. This is a verifiable correctness risk introduced by the diff (extra, potentially failing save after a side-effecting delete).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent name normalization: update does not strip group.name while create does, violating the invariant

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create the name is normalized with `(params[:name] || '').strip`, but in Admin::GroupsController#update the rename path sets `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` without stripping. This means a group created as "bob" could later be renamed to " bob ", producing inconsistent normalization/possible trailing-space names, which conflicts with the normalization behavior enforced on create (and even tested in the spec).

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and returns success_json even when zero users were added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each username is looked up; missing users are simply skipped, and the action returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it typically will even if no users were added). However, this “ignore unknown usernames and still succeed” behavior is consistent with the prior behavior in the removed incremental update path (there was even a spec asserting it “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”). So while the finding describes the behavior correctly, it is not a clear defect introduced by this diff and appears intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint limit parameter has no upper bound, allowing clients to request excessively large limits

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is set from `(params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then used directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/maximum enforced. This allows a client to pass an arbitrarily large `limit`, potentially causing very large DB queries and responses for groups the requester can see.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint runs COUNT(*) and SELECT in separate queries without a shared transaction, causing potential count drift

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` followed by a separate query `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and returns `meta.total` alongside the selected members. These are two independent SQL statements with no transaction or shared snapshot, so concurrent membership changes between them can make `meta.total` inconsistent with the returned page (count drift). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one error in totalPages calculation adds a phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (except when `user_count == 0`). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users with limit 50), `Math.floor(100/50) + 1` yields `3` even though there are only 2 pages. This creates a phantom extra page and can make `showingLast` incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: next action offset calculation caps at user_count instead of the last page boundary, potentially walking into an empty terminal page
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same pagination bug: the next offset is capped at user_count rather than the last valid page start, which can yield an empty final page when offset equals total, causing confusing UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers clamps offset to user_count instead of a valid offset boundary, resulting in empty pages

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the requested offset is clamped with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`. If `offset` becomes exactly `user_count`, the request goes out with `offset=user_count`, which yields an empty result set (offset is past the last record). The UI can drive `offset` to `user_count` via `next` action: `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"));` e.g., `user_count=100`, `limit=50`: offsets go 0 -> 50 -> 100, and the third fetch returns no members. So the finding about empty pages due to clamping to `user_count` is a real, verifiable issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, breaking the function contract and caller error handling
model.findMembers() in setupController is fire-and-forget with no error handling or loading state, causing silent failures

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`, the previous `afterModel` hook returned the `model.findMembers()` promise, meaning Ember would wait for it (triggering loading/error substates on rejection). The diff removes that and calls `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without returning/awaiting it and without any `.catch(...)`/error action wiring. As a result, failed member-load AJAX requests will not participate in route transition error handling/loading states, and the UI can remain empty without any explicit feedback beyond a console error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member does not validate if user_id corresponds to an actual user or current member, silently no-ops and returns success_json

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, without checking whether the `user_id` exists or whether the user was actually a member. However, the prior implementation (`update_patch`) also silently no-oped for non-existent users (it skipped removal if `User.find_by_username` returned nil) and still returned `success_json`, and specs even explicitly expected silent success when removing non-members. So while the lack of validation is true, it is not a clear defect introduced by this diff nor obviously incorrect given the established behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member use read-modify-write without optimistic locking or transaction, risking clobbered concurrent updates

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `add_members` iterates over provided usernames and calls `group.add(user)` for each, and `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`. These are direct association add/remove operations (i.e., they create/delete join records), not a pattern where the full membership set is read into memory, modified, and then written back wholesale. There is no “clobbering” write of a previously-read membership list (unlike a `usernames=` style setter might do). While concurrent adds/removes could race in general, the code shown does not perform a read-modify-write of the same attribute/state that would overwrite concurrent changes, and the trailing `group.save` does not re-save membership state from a stale snapshot.

adjudication_records.issue_text: find_group uses non-sargable lower(name) query causing full table scans on the hot paginated members path

adjudication.rationale: The `find_group` method still uses `Group.find_by("lower(name) = ?", name.downcase)`, but that exact pattern already existed before this diff (the diff only reindents it). The claim that it will cause full table scans on a “hot paginated members path” is not verifiable from the diff: whether it’s sargable depends on DB/indexing (e.g., a functional index on `lower(name)`), which isn’t shown here, and the diff doesn’t introduce or worsen this query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: index action uses leading-wildcard ILIKE query which is non-sargable and scans the entire table as group count grows

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#index` performing `groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%")`. The leading wildcard (`%term%`) makes the predicate non-sargable for a normal btree index on `name`, so PostgreSQL typically can’t use the index to narrow results and will scan/filter as the table grows. This behavior is directly verifiable from the query pattern present in the diff (even though the change here is just `ilike` -> `ILIKE`, the non-sargable pattern remains).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent API parameter naming: add_members and remove_member use group_id while other actions use id

adjudication.rationale: While `add_members`/`remove_member` read `params.require(:group_id)`, that matches the routes added under `resources :groups` (`/admin/groups/:group_id/members(.json)`), and the client calls also include the group id in the URL (`/admin/groups/` + id + `/members.json`). Other actions (`update`/`destroy`) correctly use `params[:id]` because their routes are `/admin/groups/:id`. This is an API naming inconsistency, but it is not a verifiable bug/defect introduced by the diff since all call sites and routes align.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers breaks promise contract for empty group names in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js: returns bare undefined instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), risking a TypeError for future callers chaining .then().

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was changed from `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]); }` to `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, which verifiably returns `undefined` on empty names. That breaks the previously consistent promise-returning behavior of the method and would cause a `TypeError` for any caller that does `findMembers().then(...)` in that case (even if the specific `.then` call sites shown in this diff were removed/changed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) in remove_member action passes an integer ID instead of a record object, which may raise an error on a has_many :through association; should look up the User record first.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer from params. For ActiveRecord `has_many` / `has_many :through` collection associations, `delete` is intended to receive record objects (or an array of records); passing an Integer commonly triggers `ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch` rather than removing the join row. A verifiable safer implementation would be `user = User.find(user_id)` then `group.users.delete(user)` (or delete via the join model).

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member action doesn't validate user existence or membership before deletion, creating inconsistent behavior compared to the add_members action which checks if the user exists.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)`, which removes a join-row by id. If the user id doesn’t exist or the user isn’t a member, this is effectively a no-op (no association row to delete) and does not create inconsistency or an invalid state. `add_members` looks up users by username to obtain ids to add, but `remove_member` can safely operate by id without a prior existence check. The proposed finding describes a stylistic/behavioral difference, not a clear defect introduced by the diff.
